quote:
Trade winds stir the same old waters; a calm leader sees the ripples before they turn to storms.

In the silence between day and night, words can be both curses and crowns—listen to the quiet in the midst of debate.

A judge’s marble tablets crumble faster than a fortress of stone when truth sleeps in the corners of judgment.

When a city’s gaze falls upon the shadow of a gunfire, the wound stains the air; only the heart can heal what no treaty can mend.

War’s footsteps echo in the bones of rivers; they nourish the soil yet poison dreams with cold ash.

Even a bird that long takes to leave a beak’s comfort seeks the distant horizon—so does the mind seek isolation from disease’s persistent breath.

A chocolate bar that shrinks as it is eaten reminds us that value measured by size is a mirage; the true taste resides within the palm.
